ядра.ядро_en: SynthID is a tool that embeds digital watermarks directly into content generated by Google's AI models; the digital watermarks are not visible to users and are used for verification purposes. Currently, it can be used to verify whether images, videos or audio were created or edited by Google AI tools.

ядра.ядро_en: The digital watermark will usually still exist even if the image, video or audio is re-scaled, re-coloured, compressed or altered in other ways. However, there's still a chance that after many alterations the watermark won't be detected.

оговорки.текст_en: SynthID 'acts as a robust watermark that remains detectable even when the content is shared or undergoes a range of transformations' (transformations not listed).

Historical (2023, Imagen): designed so it doesn't compromise image quality and remains detectable after adding filters, changing colours and saving with lossy compression (most commonly JPEG); 'isn't foolproof against extreme image manipulations'; 'While this technology isn't perfect, our internal testing shows that it's accurate against many common image manipulations'; images 'and even some edited versions' can be identified later.
Historical illustration (alt text): the watermarked image shown modified by blur, grayscale, blue tint, rotation, color filters, noise and brightness — per-edit detection results are not given.

SynthID isn't a silver bullet for identifying AI generated content; it works effectively on its own but can be combined with other AI detection approaches, and it is not built to directly stop motivated adversaries.

ядра.подтема: как читать результат SynthID: найден / не найден / неясно
ядра.ядро_en: If a SynthID watermark is detected, it means that all or part of the image was created or edited by Google's AI models. If a SynthID watermark isn't detected, it means that the image wasn't created or edited by Google AI, but it could have been created by other AI systems. In some cases it isn't clear; common reasons are 'Not enough details to watermark' (e.g. very simple or abstract content) and 'Likely too small an edit' (minor alterations might not carry a detectable watermark).
